paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think Jesus is saying with the treasure and the pearl: the kingdom of heaven is worth more than everything else you own (Matthew 13:44-46). The man in the field found the treasure, and "in his joy he went and sold all he had." The merchant found "one very precious pearl" and did the same. Nobody in either picture is dragging his feet, because when you see what it's worth, giving up the rest feels like the easy part.

Then comes the net, and Jesus gets serious. The net catches "all kinds of fish," and at the end of the age the angels "will come and separate the wicked from the righteous" (Matthew 13:47-49). I think that's a loud reminder that being near the kingdom is not the same as belonging to it. So don't just admire the treasure from a distance, baker. Take it seriously while there's still time.

Jesus finishes by asking, "Have you understood all these things?" and the disciples say, "Yes" (Matthew 13:51). Then He says a scribe who has been discipled in the kingdom is like a homeowner who brings out of his storeroom "new treasures as well as old" (Matthew 13:52). I think that means what you learn is meant to be kept and brought back out, not left in the dark like a certain stamper in a drawer. So keep filling your storeroom, friend, because the treasure is worth it. The teaching isn't over yet, either.
